```{r}

if(!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, gapminder,
               bslib, bsicons, shiny, 
               rnaturalearth, plotly, 
               countrycode, htmltools, 
               reactable, here
               )
#getting inspectdf installed
pacman::p_load_current_gh("the-graph-courses/inspectdf")

```

```{r}
#load datasets

hiv_living_raw <- read.csv(here("people_living_with_hiv_number_all_ages.csv"))
hiv_death_raw <- read.csv(here("annual_hiv_deaths_number_all_ages.csv"))

# hiv_living_raw
# hiv_death_raw
```

#data exploration- all commented out

```{r}
#data manipulation

#altering the datasets to pivot longer so I can work with them

hiv_living_long <- hiv_living_sub%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 3,names_to = "year", 
               values_to = "cases")



hiv_death_long <- hiv_death_sub%>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 3,names_to = "year", 
               values_to = "cases")

# viewing
# hiv_living_long
# hiv_death_long
  
```

```{r}
#page 1 content: people living with HIV (2011)

#first- country with highest number of people living with HIV
view(hiv_living_long)

highest_hiv_living_country <- hiv_living_long%>%
  arrange(-cases)%>%
  head(1)%>%
  pull(name)

#value
highest_hiv_living_value <- hiv_living_long%>%
  arrange(-cases)%>%
  head(1)%>%
  pull(cases)

  arrange(cases)%>%
  head(1)%>%
  pull(name)

  arrange(cases)%>%
  head(1)%>%
  pull(cases)

#interactive map of number of people living with HIV in 2011

#first create object of map/shapes
country_shapes <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries()

#now join/combine the datasets


#capitalizing geo column first
hiv_living_long <- hiv_living_long%>%
  mutate(geo = str_to_upper(geo))

#now combine datasets
country_hiv_living_combined <- left_join(country_shapes, hiv_living_long, by = c("adm0_a3" = "geo"))%>%
  mutate(tooltip_label = paste(name.y , 
                               cases, 
                               sep = ": "))

#create the map
gap_map <- ggplot(country_hiv_living_combined)+
  geom_sf(aes(fill = cases, text = tooltip_label))+
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "mistyrose", high = "darkred")+ #added this so its shades of red
  theme_void()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

#make map interactive
gapmap_ggplotly <- ggplotly(gap_map, tooltip = "text")



#graph: top 10 countries highest # of people living with hiv

#creating the dataset of top 10 countries
top_10_hiv_living <- hiv_living_long%>%
  arrange(-cases)%>%
  head(10)%>%
    mutate(tooltip_label = paste(name, 
                               cases, 
                               sep = ": "))

#creating the graph
right_graph_final <- ggplot(top_10_hiv_living, aes(y=reorder(name, cases),
                        x = cases, fill = cases, 
                        text = tooltip_label))+
  geom_col()+
  geom_text(aes(label = cases), 
            hjust = 1.1, #added this to fit the values within the bars
            color = "white")+
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "mistyrose", high = "darkred") + #added this so its shades of red
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) + #added this so the x values are not in scientific notation
  labs(y = "Country", 
       x = "Case Count")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

```{r}
#page 3 content

hiv_combined <- hiv_living_long %>%
  select(geo, name, hiv_living_long = cases) %>%
  inner_join(
    hiv_death_long %>%
      select(geo, deaths = cases),
    by = "geo"
  )

other_graph <- ggplot(hiv_combined, aes(x = hiv_living_long, y = deaths)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "People Living with HIV vs. HIV Deaths, 2011",
    x = "People Living with HIV (log scale)",
    y = "HIV Deaths (log scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

## Discussion 

::: {.card .custom-card padding="3px" expandable="false" fill="false"}

The data show a strong positive relationship between the number of people living with HIV and HIV-related deaths in 2011. Countries with more people living with HIV generally experienced more deaths, but substantial variation exists between countries with similar numbers of people living with HIV. This suggests that factors such as access to treatment and quality of healthcare may influence HIV mortality.

:::
